chunks: And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, he said:
The ʿaqiqah is obligatory when a child is born to a man. If he wishes to name him on the day of his birth, he may do so.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: the sacrificial rite performed for a newborn child
key_terms.مِنْ يَوْمِهِ: on the very day of birth

ai.seo_question: Is ʿaqiqah obligatory for a newborn, and can the child be named on the first day?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the ʿaqiqah for a newborn is obligatory and connects it directly to the birth of a child. It also permits naming the child on the very day of birth, indicating flexibility and immediacy in this family practice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4713 - In the narration of Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from the Righteous Servant (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)), that he said:
"Aqiqah is obligatory when a man is blessed with a child. If he wishes to name the child on the same day, he may do so."
